findings.text: Provides a global per-CPU initialization entry that runs only when at least one ITS node exists. It first ensures redistributor LPIs are in a safe state and then initializes per-CPU LPI structures and collections. A failure while disabling LPIs is propagated and aborts the remaining steps.

Device-tree discovery performs two sweeps over children matching the ITS compatible. The first sweep resets every available MSI controller instance before any state is built, aborting entirely if any reset fails. The second sweep skips unavailable or non-MSI nodes with a warning, initializes a node object from registers and NUMA affinity, probes it, and destroys the object on probe failure.

ITS quiescence is entered by clearing enable controls and then polling the control register until a quiescent indication appears. The poll is bounded by a decrementing counter with a tiny delay and processor relax between reads, returning busy if the bound expires. Callers use this before mapping validation, suspend, resume and reset.

Suspend saves the control value, forces quiescence, and on success also saves the command queue base; on any failure it restores the saved control for the failing node and walks already processed nodes in reverse restoring their controls. Resume re-quiesces, rewrites command base, realigns software write pointer and hardware writer, rewrites only previously valid translation tables, restores control, and reinitializes the local collection when its identifier is below the hardware collection count.

A global raw spinlock serializes traversal and mutation of the ITS node list during save, restore and probe insertion. Save and restore hold it across the whole list walk including register accesses and error unwind. Probe takes it only for list insertion after all allocation and hardware programming for that node has completed.

Probing applies vendor quirks first, then handles virtualization extensions, allocates zeroed command queue memory, allocates translation tables and collections, programs the command base, enables the hardware, creates the interrupt domain, and finally publishes the node. Any allocation or domain failure unwinds in reverse order and unmaps auxiliary windows.

Command queue base is programmed with read-allocate write-allocate write-back inner-shareable attributes plus size and valid indications. The value is read back; if shareability differs, non-shareable hardware drops both shareability and cacheability to non-cached and records that the queue needs explicit flushing, with forced non-shareable builds masking the readback before comparison.

Quirk selection matches revision identifiers with masks, device-tree properties, or machine compatibility. Effects are confined to adjusting reported identifier widths, translation entry size, message base hook, redistributor offset, shareability and cacheability, allocation flags, or recording workaround flags. The Synquacer pre-translation window derives message base from window base plus device identifier scaled by four and narrows the identifier width from window size.

Virtualization without direct move support assigns each ITS a small numeric slot from a global bitmap under an assumption of single-threaded early execution. The chosen value is written to the control field and read back; if hardware reports a different value that hardware value is adopted, and setting an already used bit is treated as a duplicate error.

Redistributor LPI shutdown first checks physical LPI support and exits successfully when already disabled, when local state shows LPIs enabled through hotplug, or when tables were preallocated. Otherwise it clears the enable bit, orders the write, polls for the write-pending indication to clear with a one-second microsecond-granularity bound, and then verifies the enable bit actually cleared, distinguishing timeout from inability to clear.

Pending-table memory handling runs exactly once per CPU, guarded by a per-redistributor done flag. A missing pending page is a warning and an out-of-memory failure. Pre-programmed tables cause the preallocated page to be freed, otherwise the page address is reserved for later kexec use. The last CPU to come up schedules a work item that removes the temporary hotplug state.

NUMA affinity for ITS instances is held as an array of pairs, each with a 32-bit NUMA node identifier and a 32-bit ITS identifier. The array and its populated count live in init memory, are filled by SRAT parsing, looked up by linear search returning a no-node sentinel on miss, and freed once after use.

Hardware windows use fixed sizes: ITS control mapping spans 64 KiB, ACPI ITS memory spans 128 KiB, virtualization SGIR window spans 64 KiB at 128 KiB offset, and one erratum forces a 128 KiB virtual redistributor offset. Device-tree matching uses compatible arm,gic-v3-its with an msi-controller boolean, and ACPI identification requires product arch values 0x30 or 0x40 in the PIDR2 arch field.

The hardware collection count is an eight-bit field extracted from the TYPER register by right shift and mask. Resume uses a comparison of local collection identifier against this count to decide whether collection state lives in the ITS and must be reinitialized.

Arriving with LPIs already enabled without hotplug or preallocation indicates probable memory corruption; the code taints the kernel, attempts damage control by disabling, and can fail with timeout if write-pending never clears or busy if the enable bit never clears. Resume with the ITS still enabled is treated as firmware breakage and warned about before forcing quiescence.

The pre-translation window breaks message isolation, so its quirk clears the isolated MSI domain flag. Forced non-shareable operation and hardware reporting non-shareable both imply command queue accesses may need explicit cache maintenance rather than relying on coherency.

Virtual processing element support prefers direct invalidation when the redistributor offers it and does nothing further. Otherwise it allocates a power-of-two sized proxy array based on possible CPU count, creates a proxy device using the largest representable device identifier, fails if allocation fails, initializes a dedicated lock and victim index, and records the usable slot count from the created device.

A new ITS node object is zeroed, its spinlock mutex and list heads initialized, TYPER read, base and physical base stored, message base helper set to the default, MSI domain flags set to isolated plus immutable, and NUMA node plus firmware handle attached. Destruction only unmaps the control window and frees the object; mapping failure yields null without allocation.

SRAT ITS affinity entries are counted first; non-positive counts abort without allocation. Each entry is length-checked, its proximity domain translated to a NUMA node, out-of-range nodes rejected with an error log but without aborting the walk, and valid entries appended with an informational log of proximity domain to ITS to node.
Power management registers suspend and resume callbacks through a syscore operations structure and containing syscore object, binding save-disable to suspend and restore-enable to resume.

Interrupt domain creation builds a hierarchical MSI domain with firmware handle, ITS operations, configured domain flags and a fixed parent, plus heap-allocated MSI info binding ITS operations and the node pointer. Failure to create the parent domain frees the info and reports out-of-memory.
